summary: Klaus Wille is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997) and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter (attested 2000–2009 and 2018–2026).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn and completed his Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (2004). He has served as a professor at the University of Vienna (attested 2012–2013).

Klaus-Josef Notz (1942–2013) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Philosophisch-Theologische Hochschule Benediktbeuern (1966–1971) and earned his Doctor theologiae from the University of Munich (1978–1984), where he served as Lehrbeauftragter in 1996.

Klemens Karlsson is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at Uppsala University by 2000, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Peter Schalk (attested 1999).

Knut A. Jacobsen (born 1956) works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at UC Santa Barbara (~1990–1994) and served as Professor in the History of Religions at the University of Bergen (1996) and professor at the University of Oslo (attested 1999).

Kobun Otogawa (1938–2002) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Komazawa University, under Gadjin Nagao at Kyoto University, and at Eihei-ji. He held posts at Tassajara Zen Mountain Center (1967–1970), Haiku Zendo (1970–1978), and Naropa University (2001).

Kodai Akino (1858–1934) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari at Komazawa University. He served at Komazawa University in administrative roles, becoming president (学長) in 1909, and lectured at the University of Tokyo.

Kodo Kawamura (1933–2022) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his master's (~1956–1958) and doctorate (1984) at Komazawa University, where he also served as a professor from circa 1966 to 2004.

Kodo Sawaki (1880–1965) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Koho Sawada, Zenko Sawada, and Sotan Oka. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji (~1949–1965).
Kodo Yamada (1866–1933) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who taught at both Komazawa University and Keio University.
Kodo Yotsuya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Komazawa University under Shiro Matsumoto and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg.

Koen Wellens specializes in Sinology, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under Charles Willemen at Ghent University and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo under doctoral supervisor Per Kværne.
Koenraad Elst (born 1959) is a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and Sinology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1988–1993) and completed an MA at KU Leuven (~1988–1999).

Kogen Mizuno (1901–2006) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo (1928). He held professorships at the University of Tokyo and Komazawa University, where he became president in 1976.

Kogi Kudara (1945–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1979) and worked as an editor for the Ryukoku Buddhist Society (attested 2002).
Koichi Furusaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Hakuyu Hadano. He served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University (attested 1991).
Koichi Hiraoka (born 1961) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University. He holds a post as a visiting professor at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).

Koichi Hokazono (born 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD from Kyushu University, where he held a post (attested 1995); he was also a professor at The International University of Kagoshima (attested 1991–2000).

Koichi Hoshina (1872–1955) was a scholar in linguistics and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897), where he later held a post (~1902), and worked at Tokyo University of Education (~1903–1932).

Koichi Shinohara (born 1941) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He was a professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004), coordinator at the University of Toronto Mississauga (attested 2004), and a senior lecturer in religious studies at Yale University (~2004–2021).
